draft.title: The endocrine system
card: The endocrine system is made up of glands. Glands release chemical messengers called hormones.
Hormones travel in the blood. They reach cells all around the body, but they only affect cells that can respond to them.
Hormone messages are slower than nerve messages, because blood carries them. Their effects often last longer, from minutes to hours or more.
Insulin is a hormone released by the pancreas when blood glucose rises after a meal. It lowers blood glucose, and its effects build up over minutes to hours.
draft.remember: Hormones are slower than nerves, but their effects often last longer.

a.q: A gland releases a hormone. How does the hormone reach the cells it affects?
a.why: Glands release hormones into the blood, and the blood carries them around the body. Neurons carry nerve impulses, not hormones, so travelling along neurons is a common mix-up.
a.clue: Think about what the body uses to carry things around.

b.q: Mia eats a big meal and her blood glucose rises. The pancreas releases insulin, and her glucose falls slowly over the next hour or two. What best explains this?
opts: Hormone effects are slower and last longer than nerves
Insulin is a hormone, so it acts faster than nerve messages
Insulin is carried along neurons to the body cells
The pancreas sends the message as a quick electrical impulse
b.why: Insulin is a hormone. It travels in the blood, so it acts more slowly than a nerve message, and its effects last longer. That is why glucose falls over minutes to hours. Hormones do not travel along neurons, and they are not quick electrical impulses.
b.clue: Compare the speed and length of hormone effects with nerve effects.

b.best: Hormone effects are slower and last longer than nerves
